motion: The college should open its fabrication workshop to residents
own_claim: Public workshop access requires safe supervision and reliable funding.
own_opening: Public workshop access requires safe supervision and reliable funding.

prior_history.content: The workshop could be open to all residents every evening, with access to every machine. Shared tools would let people repair belongings.
Who would supervise inexperienced users, and which department would fund consumables?

chunks: Residents would have access to every machine. To be precise about this proposal, access is to hand tools in one supervised Saturday session, not to powered cutting equipment.
Participation would be by reservation for adults who complete an induction. College classes keep their existing priority.
I accept publishing the supervision rota before reservations open. Funding for consumables is still unsettled.
The independent benefit is an opportunity to repair belongings with shared hand tools. That possibility does not establish how much money participants will save.
checks: Recognizes access is limited to hand tools in a supervised Saturday session, not access to every machine each evening
Does not claim supervision disclosure was refused, or treat an unestablished savings figure as the current case
Engages the unresolved consumables funding or adequacy of supervision while acknowledging the repair opportunity

motion: The village should introduce a shared parcel pickup counter
own_claim: A pickup counter must preserve access for people who cannot travel.
own_opening: A pickup counter must preserve access for people who cannot travel.

prior_history.content: A shared counter at the village hall could simplify deliveries. Households would collect there rather than receive home delivery.
What happens to residents unable to travel, and who is responsible for uncollected parcels?
I accept continued home delivery on request for residents unable to travel, without requiring medical evidence. That access condition is part of the proposal.
That addresses an access condition, but responsibility for uncollected parcels still needs agreement.

chunks: The practical proposal is a six-week optional counter at the hall, with no collection fee.
Existing delivery arrangements continue for households that do not opt in. The access condition we already agreed remains in force.
A counter could reduce repeated delivery attempts for participants, but I have no measured reduction to offer.
Responsibility for uncollected parcels remains open and must be settled before the counter opens.
checks: Recognizes the six-week optional trial without a collection fee
Acknowledges home delivery on request for residents unable to travel, rather than proposing it as a concession the opponent has refused
Engages responsibility for uncollected parcels as a pre-opening condition without inventing measured delivery savings

motion: The district should extend the community garden opening hours
own_claim: Evening access needs staffing and protection for neighbors.
own_opening: Evening access needs staffing and protection for neighbors.

prior_history.content: The garden should remain open until ten every night. Evening access would help residents with daytime jobs.
Late noise could affect neighbors, and the staffing plan is unspecified.
I withdraw the ten-o-clock opening proposal. Keep the current closing time while we investigate staffing.
The independent question of access for daytime workers remains worth discussing.

chunks: After speaking with the volunteer group, I again propose later opening, but only until eight on Fridays for a four-week trial.
No amplified sound would be allowed, and the trial depends on a named volunteer being present for each session.
I accept recording neighbor complaints and publishing them at the end of the trial; no claim of neighborhood approval has been established.
If a session has no volunteer, it closes at the existing time. Volunteer reliability remains the question to resolve.
checks: Recognizes the current reasserted proposal is Friday opening until eight for four weeks, not the withdrawn nightly ten-o-clock proposal
Acknowledges the volunteer condition and existing-time fallback when no volunteer is available
Engages volunteer reliability or complaint review without claiming neighborhood approval or that amplified sound is permitted

motion: The market should install a public drinking-water station
own_claim: Public facilities need accountable maintenance and a justified budget.
own_opening: Public facilities need accountable maintenance and a justified budget.

prior_history.content: A water station would eliminate plastic bottle waste at the market. It would also offer drinking water to people who bring no bottle.
A refill station cannot eliminate all bottle waste. Who cleans it and tests the supply?

chunks: The waste point needs to be more modest: some visitors might refill, but no amount of waste reduction is established.
The access proposal is one station with a drinking spout at the north entrance for an eight-week trial, not a market-wide rollout.
I agree that the cleaning rota and water-testing responsibility must be published before installation.
The installation budget and who pays for replacement parts remain unresolved. The access benefit stands separately from any waste estimate.
checks: Recognizes one station at the north entrance for an eight-week trial
Does not treat elimination of all bottle waste as still asserted or as disproving the independent drinking-water access benefit
Engages installation or replacement-parts funding without claiming cleaning and testing disclosure were refused

motion: The town should expand access to its local history archive
own_claim: An archive expansion needs durable staffing and clear handling rules.
own_opening: An archive expansion needs durable staffing and clear handling rules.

prior_history.content: The archive would open on Saturdays. It would provide large-print finding aids. School groups could book visits. A quiet research desk would be available.
Opening hours need staffing, and school visits must not displace ordinary readers.
Readers could request digital scans. Fragile originals would stay supervised. A catalogue terminal would be available. An oral-history listening point is another independent benefit.
Scanning needs permission checks. The terminal needs maintenance, and headphones need cleaning.

I accept permission checks before scans are released. I accept publishing a terminal-maintenance contact. Volunteers could guide first-time visitors. A noticeboard could advertise local history events.
Those commitments answer disclosure questions. How would shifts be filled, and what can happen if a volunteer cancels?

chunks: Saturday opening is now a six-Saturday trial with two booked research places per session. School visits remain by separate appointment.
All the access ideas remain options, but the immediate request funds only the supervised research desk and finding aids. Scanning and the listening point need separate costings.
A named archivist must approve handling of fragile originals. Permission checks still precede release of any later scans.
Staffing the six sessions is unresolved. A canceled session must be rescheduled or refunded; funding for that guarantee has not been identified.
checks: Recognizes the immediate six-Saturday trial with two booked research places per session
Acknowledges current funding covers the supervised research desk and finding aids, while scanning and the listening point require separate costings
Engages unresolved staffing or the reschedule/refund guarantee without claiming permission checks or fragile-item supervision were rejected

motion: The housing association should improve the shared courtyard
own_claim: Courtyard changes must preserve access and assign maintenance fairly.
own_opening: Courtyard changes must preserve access and assign maintenance fairly.

prior_history.content: The courtyard could have benches, planters, a book exchange and a drinking tap. Each serves a different need.
Benches must leave the access path clear, and plants need someone responsible for watering.
A shaded seat could help on hot days. A noticeboard could advertise meetings. A bicycle repair stand could support riders. A rain barrel could supply planters.
The repair stand needs inspection, and stagnant stored water raises a maintenance question.
I accept keeping the access path clear and naming a planter-waterer before planting. A chess table is another option. A small chalk area and a wildlife sign could support informal learning.
Who will pay for inspections and cleaning? Listing several attractive uses does not resolve upkeep.

chunks: The actual funding request is for two benches and three planters for a three-month trial. The other ideas stay on a future-options list.
There will be no rain barrel in this trial. The benches must leave the agreed access path clear, and planting waits for a named waterer.
I accept a public cleaning rota before installation, but the replacement budget for damaged items has not been agreed.
The possible benefit is somewhere to sit and grow plants. I have no evidence that these changes would increase property values.
checks: Recognizes two benches and three planters for a three-month trial, rather than immediate implementation of all listed options
Acknowledges the clear access path and named-waterer condition, and does not attack a rain barrel as part of the current trial
Engages the unresolved replacement budget without asserting property-value gains or treating the cleaning rota as refused

motion: The recreation center should offer equipment loans
own_claim: Equipment loans need transparent allocation and an affordable loss policy.
own_opening: Equipment loans need transparent allocation and an affordable loss policy.

prior_history.content: The center could lend footballs, rackets, walking poles and picnic blankets. Different groups would benefit from different items.
Allocation must be fair when demand exceeds supply, and damaged equipment must be checked.
Board games could serve indoor groups. Exercise mats could help classes. A pump could support cyclists. A folding cart could help people carry supplies.
Which items would be available to begin with? The list exceeds the stated storage room.
I accept publishing an allocation rule. Rackets would be inspected between loans. A repair kit, a stopwatch and a set of cones are additional possibilities.
Who pays for losses, and would a large deposit exclude people with little spare money?

chunks: The first phase lends only balls and board games for one school term, with loans lasting up to two days. All other items need a later storage decision.
I accept no cash deposit during the trial. That does not mean lost items have no replacement cost.
Borrowers would receive the published allocation rule before booking, and items would be checked when returned.
The source of the replacement fund is still undecided. Access to shared games is a reason to consider the trial, not evidence that it pays for itself.
checks: Recognizes only balls and board games for one school term, with loans up to two days
Acknowledges the no-cash-deposit trial and published allocation rule rather than accusing the opponent of imposing a large deposit
Engages the unfunded replacement cost without treating the trial as already self-financing or attacking storage for all future items

motion: The museum should improve visitor assistance
own_claim: Visitor assistance should be accessible and have a sustainable staffing plan.
own_opening: Visitor assistance should be accessible and have a sustainable staffing plan.

prior_history.content: The museum could provide printed maps, a staffed welcome desk, audio directions and large-print labels. These address different visitor needs.
Audio directions do not help everyone, and welcome staffing must not remove gallery supervision.
A tactile orientation board is another option. Visitors could borrow stools. A quiet waiting area could help groups. Translated leaflets could support more languages.
Which translations are justified by demand? Stools also need safe storage and cleaning.
I accept retaining printed directions alongside audio. I accept keeping gallery supervision separate. A family trail, a volunteer tour and a suggestions box are additional options.
A trial needs a limited scope, and the people providing assistance need appropriate training.

chunks: The immediate proposal is a welcome desk and printed maps on four weekend mornings. The other ideas require later decisions.
Assistance would be optional and free. Existing gallery supervision stays at its current level, with separate volunteers at the desk.
Volunteers must complete an orientation session before serving visitors. The training provider and budget remain undecided.
This may make arrival easier for some visitors; I am not claiming an increase in ticket sales. The independent access benefit should be considered alongside the staffing cost.
checks: Recognizes a welcome desk and printed maps on four weekend mornings, rather than an immediate rollout of every listed option
Acknowledges optional free assistance and separate desk volunteers without a reduction in gallery supervision
Engages the unresolved training provider or budget without asserting ticket-sale gains or claiming training is not required
